headline: Brent Crude Trades Near $116 as Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia Reignite Supply Fears
summary: Brent oil futures climbed 1.62% to $115.70 per barrel in early Asian trade following renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and falling inventories, stoking regional supply concerns.
why: Crude oil is a critical global commodity whose price moves affect inflation, central bank policy, and operating margins across industrial, transport, and consumer sectors worldwide.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Heightened security risks to Saudi Arabian infrastructure threaten Middle Eastern crude exports, reducing global supply cushions.

impacts.name: Airlines
impacts.why: Rising crude oil prices translate directly into higher jet fuel costs, compressing carrier operating margins.

why_moved: Crude futures advanced as attacks against Saudi targets raised the threat of disruptions in the world's primary oil-exporting region, compounded by declining inventories.
